newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-NOT EVEN FALDO SURE OF RYDER CUP PLACE - BALLESTEROS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NOT EVEN FALDO SURE OF RYDER CUP PLACE - BALLESTEROS.

text.p: European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros reminded Nick Faldo on Thursday that he was not guaranteed a Ryder Cup place.

Ballesteros, who will mastermind Europe's defence against the Americans in Valderrama at the end of September, said even players of Faldo's calibre could not be sure of selection if they did not make the team automatically.
That means being in the top 10 at the end of the BMW International Open on August 31, after which Ballesteros will select the final two for the September 26-28 clash.
"I have made it very clear that I shall pick the players who I think are best for the team," he said.
"For me there are no friends. I want the best players on the team. I shall make the decision from that. On that there is no question."

Ballesteros, speaking on the eve of the prestigious British PGA championship at Wentworth, said he was pleased to see Faldo, the lynchpin of Europe's victory at Oak Hill in 1995, playing this week to try to secure Cup points.
"Obviously it is good that Nick is playing here, and at the Open, also the Irish Open and Loch Lomond," Ballesteros said.
"So he has four good chances to make points and also the U.S. Open and PGA. So he still has a chance to make the team automatically."
Ballesteros said he did not ask Faldo to play at Wentworth this week to gain points. "Maybe he is a little worried about his selection."
Faldo, who is based on the U.S. Tour, is currently 62nd on the qualifying list.
He said on Wednesday that he had come to try to earn points at Wentworth after failing to collect any at last month's U.S. Masters where, as defending champion, he missed the cut.
Ballesteros's compatriot Jose Maria Olazabal said he was surprised to have done as well since making his comeback from serious foot problems three months ago.

In seven tournaments after 18 months away from the game, Olazabal has won once, been second, fourth, 11th, 12th twice and 22nd to reach fourth place on the money list and 11th place in the Ryder Cup standings.
"I'm very surprised how well I have done," he said. "I thought it would take me longer to get to a high level. It is a miracle, if you believe in miracles.
"When I came back, I was more concerned about my feet than my score or my swing.
"Now I have got to the point where I am more concerned with my score than my health. I cannot blame my feet anymore," he said.
